verdict.rationale: Galileo ships its own MCP server, which lets AI IDEs such as Cursor or Copilot drive core operations like creating datasets, running experiments and setting up prompt templates. It also has an in-product AI Assistant for troubleshooting and accepts natural-language feedback to tune metrics. Natural-language operation therefore exists, but mostly through external AI clients or narrow features. missing for 10: a documented in-product natural-language command interface covering general operations, detail on the AI Assistant's scope beyond troubleshooting, hands-on or independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: With MCP, you can access Galileo's capabilities directly from your development environment, including: Creating and managing datasets, Running experiments, Setting up prompt templates

The Galileo Model Context Protocol (MCP) server enables seamless integration between AI-powered IDEs, such as Cursor, or VS Code with GitHub Copilot, and Galileo's evaluation and observability platform.
Troubleshoot your agentic system with the AI Assistant.
This allows you to continuously provide feedback in natural language that automatically improves the metrics
